synonyms: Rhus canadensis var. trilobata (Nutt.) A.Gray ex J.M.Coult.
taxonomic_note: Current Kew accepts Rhus aromatica Aiton and treats Rhus trilobata Nutt. and Rhus canadensis var. trilobata as synonyms of Rhus aromatica var. aromatica. Older Texas literature also uses R. aromatica var./subsp. flabelliformis. The learner keeps one species-level canonical entry and records those historical names as synonyms.
look_here_first: Count leaflets first: fragrant sumac has exactly 3. The leaflets are often fan-shaped, lobed or coarsely toothed on a low suckering deciduous shrub.

best_field_traits: low winter-deciduous clump-forming or suckering shrub
leaflets often fan-shaped, lobed or coarsely toothed
compact yellowish flowers appear before or with new leaves
female plants produce dark-red hairy drupes
morphology_keys.leaf_morphology: Ovate to obovate/fan-shaped leaflets, often shallowly to deeply lobed and crenate/coarsely toothed.
morphology_keys.inflorescence: Compact yellowish catkin-like clusters before or with leaf-out.
morphology_keys.safety_comparison: The Anacardiaceae audit explicitly warns against 'leaves of three = poison ivy.' Use habit, leaflet shape/petiolules and fruit architecture; do not test by sap contact.

comparisons.key_distinctions: R. aromatica = exactly 3 leaflets, often fan-shaped/lobed/toothed, low suckering shrub. R. microphylla has many much smaller leaflets on a compound leaf and belongs to drier western/southwestern habitats.
